description: Complete medical device invention with all parameters needed for simulation request. Expected status: SIMULATION_READY

automated_invention_candidate.target_constraint: Must detect occlusions within 2 minutes to prevent insulin overdose or underdose
automated_invention_candidate.observed_phenomenon: Piezoelectric pressure sensors in microfluidic channels show measurable voltage spikes when flow is obstructed
source_mechanisms: Piezoelectric effect in PZT thin films generates voltage proportional to pressure changes
Flow obstruction in microchannels creates pressure wave reflections detectable by embedded sensors

exact_evidence_spans.span_text: Piezoelectric pressure sensors demonstrated detection of flow occlusions in microfluidic channels with response time <30 seconds

automated_invention_candidate.mechanism: Embedding piezoelectric pressure sensors in the infusion pump's fluid path enables real-time occlusion detection through pressure wave monitoring
automated_invention_candidate.cross_domain_connection: Microfluidic pressure sensing mechanism from lab-on-chip devices transfers to insulin pump occlusion detection
automated_invention_candidate.proposed_intervention: Integrate PZT thin-film piezoelectric pressure sensor downstream of pump head, with signal processing to detect pressure spikes characteristic of occlusion events
automated_invention_candidate.expected_causal_effect: Occlusion events generate pressure waves detected by PZT sensor within 30 seconds, triggering alarm before dangerous insulin delivery deviation occurs
automated_invention_candidate.falsification_test: Measure time-to-detection for induced occlusions at various flow rates; if detection time exceeds 2 minutes in >5% of trials, hypothesis is falsified

prior_art_coverage.coverage_notes: Search covered major scientific databases but not comprehensive patent search

geometry_requirements.description: Microfluidic channel with integrated PZT sensor membrane
simplifications: Assume rigid channel walls except sensor membrane

simulation_request.predicted_mechanism: Pressure wave reflection from occlusion site creates measurable deflection of PZT membrane

baseline_control.description: Standard infusion pump without integrated pressure sensor
baseline_control.reference_design: Current peristaltic pump with motor current monitoring only

success_criterion.description: Peak voltage must exceed 0.1V for reliable detection above noise floor

falsification_criterion.condition: If peak voltage output is less than 0.05V for standard occlusion event

expected_outcome.reason: All required parameters present, falsifiable prediction with measurable outcome specified
